variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Read the requested cube color and repetition count from the goal each time. Let N be twice the repetition count; for 'move ... right-side target, then put it down on the left-side target', N is 2. Update completed_target_visits from the observed interval before selecting the next subgoal. Right means the smaller-x target and left means the larger-x target, irrespective of y. Start with A, pointing at the instructed cube on the table. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits is less than N, choose B: point at the right target if the count is even, or the left target if it is odd. This also governs the transition from pickup to the first target move and between successive target moves. Select a point on the target itself, not the elevated cube or wrist. Use the latest clear view of that target anywhere in the current observed interval if it is occluded in the final scene; in particular, episode 72's first right target is visible earlier in the pickup interval. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits equals N, choose C to lower and release it on the table at the final left target. When the count equals N and the final scene shows the cube released and the hand empty, choose D. Thus release precedes button pressing even when the goal only explicitly says to press the button after the repetitions. For an unexpected dropped cube before N, choose A at the instructed cube and retain the count. For an unconfirmed arrival while still holding the cube, repeat B toward the destination selected by count parity without incrementing the count. If a required object is obscured, use its latest clear position in the current interval; if none is available, choose the best-supported location from the visible scene rather than inventing a completed visit or stopping to ask. All points use [y, x].

fields.name: completed_target_visits
fields.description: With empty incoming memory, write 0. Otherwise start with the incoming integer. The next countable destination is the smaller-x target when that integer is even, and the larger-x target when it is odd. Increase once if the observed interval shows completion of a move above that destination: the cube remains grasped, the final hand is hovering at approximately 0.100 height above that target, and that destination is highlighted at the final scene. Use the final destination rather than a stale highlight during transit. Do not count pickup, which ends with the hand raised at approximately 0.150 height, or release, which ends with an open empty hand. Do not count multiple frames of the same arrival, and do not increase beyond the required number of visits (twice the requested repetition count, or two for the instruction to go right then put down left). Otherwise preserve the incoming integer. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Integer counting completed moves above targets while holding the instructed cube, in the required alternating order starting with the robot's right target. Initialize to 0. Increase by one at the decision step immediately following each completed target move; do not increase for pickup, release, or button pressing. Count each completed move once, not each frame showing a highlight. Episode 44 and episode 72 have values [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4]; episode 53 has [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6]; episodes 56 and 69 have [0, 0, 1, 2, 2]. e.g. 2
